subject: Re: Aurora capacity ramp — multi‑year prepay & milestone billing
messages:
From: Elena Rodriguez <elena@auroraanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.legal@auroraanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora capacity ramp — multi-year prepay & milestone billing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this meeting last week. Aurora is planning a multi-year Dedicated deployment and we want to align on a prepay + milestone billing structure that matches our engineering rollout windows. High level: target committed capacity of ~1,000 TPM-equivalent (we estimate this maps to ~120 sustained GPU units under your sizing guidance) over a 3-year horizon, with most of the consumption concentrated in year 1 and year 2 as we ramp product.

Key asks from our side:
- A clear ramp schedule (tranches) tied to delivery milestones so we can release funding from our procurement budget quarterly.
- Discount tiers for annual prepay vs full 3-year prepaid.
- True-up and frontload options (ability to pull capacity forward if we hit adoption earlier).
- Standard SLA and remedies for capacity shortfalls.

Can you sketch a working proposal and include an example invoice cadence we can share with finance & legal? Attaching the internal ramp forecast spreadsheet for reference (we'll expect Redwood to propose the billing triggers).

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rodriguez
Head of Cloud Ops — Aurora Analytics
Attachment: aurora_ramp_forecast_q3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena@auroraanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora capacity ramp — multi‑year prepay & milestone billing

Elena — appreciate the details and the forecast. Ive sketched a pragmatic structure that keeps billing aligned to your quarterly procurement windows while protecting Redwood on delivery. Summary (high level):

- Term: 3 years (36 months) with two purchase options: (A) Annual prepay (invoice at start of each 12‑month period), or (B) Full 3‑year prepay (single invoice with additional discount).
- Ramp tranches (example): T1 = 40% of total committed capacity deployed by month 3; T2 = additional 30% by month 12; T3 = final 30% by month 24. We call this the "epochal" ramp playbook — tranches map to milestones you control (prod launch, regional rollouts).
- Frontload: optional frontload of up to +15% capacity in year 1 for an additional one‑time fee, with automatic amortized credit if utilisation remains below forecast.
- True‑up: 60‑day rolling true‑up window at each annual anniversary (customer pays incremental usage above committed units; refunds are not provided but can be applied as credits toward subsequent tranches).

Im attaching a first draft of the schedule and a sample invoice calendar (Aurora_Ramp_Draft_v1.xlsx). Ben — can you confirm the commercial discount bands we can offer for (A) vs (B)? Grace — FYI on the frontload credit mechanics; curious if finance prefers milestone invoicing or an escrow approach.

Next: I can turn this into a short term sheet for signature once we agree on discounting and invoice triggers.

Regards,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Aurora_Ramp_Draft_v1.xlsx (proposal stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora capacity ramp — multi‑year prepay & milestone billing

Karthik — thanks, this is a good start. Quick commercial thoughts:

- Discounting:
  - Annual prepay: baseline list less 22% for 12‑month prepay at committed units.
  - Full 3‑year prepay: we can step to ~32% discount if Aurora prepays the full committed spend up front.
  - If Aurora chooses staged milestones + escrowed funds (invoiced against milestones), offer 28% effective discount (midpoint) to reflect reduced cash certainty.

- Onramp credits & amortization: Offer an "onramp credit" that offsets up to 15% of first‑year overprovision; credit amortizes monthly against consumed capacity and expires at year end. This ensures we don't carry stranded capacity indefinitely.

- SLA and remedies: include capacity delivery SLAs for each tranche with a service credit schedule (small % credit, not punitive). If we cannot deliver a tranche on the agreed date, automatic fallback to a compatible model tier and priority scheduling for the next 30 days.

Lauren — can we support milestone invoicing (e.g., 40% on signing, 30% on T2 activation, 30% on T3 activation) from an accounting perspective? If escrow is required by procurement, what minimal language do we need in the order form?

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora capacity ramp — multi‑year prepay & milestone billing

Ben/Karthik — we can support milestone invoicing; a few finance notes to keep procurement moving:

- Milestone invoicing model: 40% due on signing (recognize as deferred revenue until delivery), 30% due on activation of T2 (recognize on activation), 30% due on activation of T3. For full 3‑yr prepay we will still record deferred revenue and amortize to revenue over the committed term; compliance is straightforward.
- Escrow: we can accept escrowed funds if Aurora requires them for governance. Minimal doc language: escrow release triggers tied to specific activation events (IP/ops signoff), and a capped release window (30 days) to avoid prolonged fund locks. Legal will need to sign off; Marcuss team may want a standard escrow addendum.
- DocuSign flow: we prefer a single order form with an Appendix A that lists tranche dates and invoice amounts. Link to the CRM deal is here: https://redwood.app/deals/ACCT-1247.

Grace — for the frontload credit mechanics: finance prefers the credit be issued as a time‑bounded consumption credit (applies for 12 months) rather than a refundable cash credit — simpler for accounting.

I can draft the Appendix A language and a short escrow addendum for Marcus.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena@auroraanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lee <marcus.legal@auroraanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora capacity ramp — multi‑year prepay & milestone billing

Elena — circling back with a consolidated proposal based on our internal alignment. Attached is Aurora_Ramp_Draft_v2.xlsx with the updated term sheet. High points: 

- Option 1 (Annual prepay): 12‑month invoices at 22% discount, milestone billing aligned to your procurement windows; tranches executed as activation events.
- Option 2 (Full 3‑yr prepay): single invoice with 32% discount; revenue amortization across 36 months on our side.
- Staged (Escrow + Milestones): 28% effective discount if funds are escrowed and released on activation; this is the middle ground that smooths cash for you and risk for us.
- Ramp tranches (epochal model): T1 = 40% by month 3, T2 = +30% by month 12, T3 = +30% by month 24. Frontload: optional +15% in Y1 with a time‑bounded consumption credit (12 months).
- True‑up: annual 60‑day window at each anniversary.
- SLA & fallback: per‑tranche delivery SLA with modest service credits and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if capacity is delayed.

Next steps: please review the attached sheet and indicate which option Aurora prefers. If you want escrow language, Marcus, Lauren will share an addendum draft. Once Aurora confirms, we will push the order form and DocuSign link.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Aurora_Ramp_Draft_v2.xlsx (proposal stub)
